properties.name: A seat learns the shared record moved when it ORIENTS, not when it writes
properties.statement:
When another contributor's work has arrived in the shared design record and this graph has never seen it, the seat is told so at the point it orients itself — not at the point it tries to write, hours later.

WHY THE MOMENT IS THE REQUIREMENT AND NOT AN ERGONOMIC PREFERENCE: the signal already existed and was already correct. `provenance::last_synced` was maintained by both the export and import paths, and `sync::assess_overwrite` already turned it into a three-way verdict. It was consulted in exactly one place — inside `export_graph`. So the design knew at the first moment of a session and spoke at the last, by which point the session had done its work against a record it did not know had moved.

WHAT SATISFYING THIS MUST NOT COST: silence during ordinary work. A seat that is merely AHEAD of the record — unexported work in progress — is the normal state of every working session and must never be reported, or the signal is ignored inside a week. The distinguishing test is whether the RECORD moved, not whether the two differ.

AND IT REPORTS RATHER THAN ACTS: taking the arrived work in is an upsert over live session state, so it stays the human's call.

⚠️ WORDING IS AN AGENT'S DRAFT. Anthony chose the MECHANISM (option A, 2026-08-11) and directed the build; he has not ruled on this statement's text, which is why this sits at `proposed`.
